definition: USMC decision doctrine: act on ~70% of the information rather than wait for certainty. Popularized by Corps Business; Jeff Bezos uses the same logic.
The documented tendency (Adams et al., 2021, Nature) to improve systems by adding elements even when subtracting works better. The master skill of the corpus is noticing what to remove.
A designed repair cycle: miss → catch-up slot → cause review → one system tweak. Each failure makes the next streak longer.
The selection process that decides what your awareness lets in. Tuned by beliefs and goals — see the gorilla experiment and 'what you focus on, you find'.
Planning from a dated, specific ending and reversing the path to today. 'If you can't name step seven, it isn't a plan.'
Therapy model, strongly supported (Dimidjian et al., 2006): scheduling meaningful action precedes and generates motivation. Action first, mood follows.
Quarterly protocol for testing a limiting belief as a behavioral experiment: act as if the opposite were true for 30 days, measure an objective outcome.
Three-week protocol rebuilding the ability to sit with stimulation-free experience: label triggers, run 30-minute no-stimulation blocks, replace one compulsion.
Temporarily adopting the posture, pace and phrasing of someone who embodies a state you don't yet have; repaid with repetition until owned.
The hours between a missed day and your return. Success is not the absence of failure; it is the speed of the comeback.
The invisible loading phase of progress — repeated work with no visible movement, ending in a phase change (the 'sudden' breakthrough).
The contested but patterned finding that decision quality degrades over long sessions (parole judge study, 2011). Practical rule: make big decisions early and fresh.
The brain's background processing during rest. The resting mind integrates what focused blocks built — one reason rest is part of the work.
Focused, goal-directed repetition with feedback. Real and powerful, but its payoff varies by domain (26% of variance in games, <1% in professions).
Refusing to let current evidence set your ceiling — acting before the proof exists. Mental rehearsal with permission; tested by measurement, not faith.
Purpose recovery: ask what life needs from you and what you once lost hours to; convert the answer into a dated 12-month mission.
The honest version of the dopamine fast: a behavioral reset (stimulus control, exposure-response prevention) — not a receptor reset, for which there is no evidence.
The 'willpower fuel tank' model. Failed a 23-lab replication; treat willpower as mood, attention and habit, not a tank.
A five-minute audit for incoming claims: state X causes Y at magnitude M; ask if the study is real, applies to you, and matches its own numbers.
Lighten, level, lean: remove what doesn't matter, match task difficulty to skill (+1), do one thing fully in a protected block.
Deep absorption in a task matched to skill (Csikszentmihalyi). Real and valuable; the '5x productivity' McKinsey figure is folklore.
The hunger hormone. In the milkshake study, its decline responded to the label ('indulgent' vs 'sensible') more than to the shake itself.
Simons & Chabris (1999): half of observers miss a person in a gorilla suit while counting passes — inattentional blindness, the basis of the attention-filter idea.
Your intrinsic worth, independent of results. Issues daily by you; the world cannot grade it.
Belief that ability can be developed. Real but modest effects (r ≈ .10; d ≈ .08): a small lever, especially for struggling students.
The repeatable stack: output-level clarity targeting, environment lockdown, timeboxing, and the perfect week underneath.
Material-science analogy used in the corpus: a system's response remembers its loading history. The unseen architecture remembers every rep.
Failing to see what you're not attending to — the gorilla. The mechanism behind 'what you focus on, you find.'
The identity-based floor that holds when a streak breaks: one miss is an abstention, not a cancelled election.
Five-layer model: physiology → state → identity → language → reality. Built from the floor up; verbs, not nouns.
James Clear's metaphor: every action is a vote for the identity you are becoming. Elections are won by consistency, not landslides.
The compound growth curve: flat for a long time, then steep. The lag is the J-curve's flat phase — where most people quit.
Inoculation against quitting during invisible growth: track leading inputs daily, lagging outputs monthly, and assume you are earlier on the curve than feels fair.
The chapter-12 metaphor: smooth, directed effort (laminar) versus scattered, dissipating effort (turbulent). Effortless = friction-free, not effort-free.
Desire is the signal, belief the amplifier, behavior the bridge, the field a mirror. The bridge is the only quadrant touching the world.
'Everything reflects your state' — decoded: confirmation bias wearing a costume. The filter admits what belief predicts, so the world appears to mirror you.
Bad events, feedback and emotions outweigh good ones of equal magnitude (Baumeister et al., 2001). Direction is settled; specific ratios (40x, 5:1, 3:1) are not.
A floor rule from a 2013 Reddit post: never let a day pass without one action toward the person you're becoming. Not a study; a sound behavioral rule.
Wanting the goal fully while releasing the timing and shape of the outcome. Reduces desperate behavior (scarcity) and improves decision quality.
Skill + problem + channel: one skill meeting one group's specific problem through one channel. Assembled in a day; compounded over years.
The day's single critical task, chosen before anything else, executed in a closed winner's loop. Everything else is maintenance.
An unplanned, unfinished goal that keeps intruding on attention until discharged or written as a next action (Masicampo & Baumeister, 2011).
A placebo given openly — still effective (Kaptchuk et al., 2010). Expectation, ritual and meaning carry much of the placebo effect.
External, measurable outcomes — results, rankings, revenue. Real and necessary; the world grades it. The trap is fusing it with the green line.
The replicated pull to resume interrupted tasks — the motivational core that survived the Zeigarnik memory claim's replication failures.
The 80/20 observation: most results come from a minority of inputs. A guide for subtraction audits, not a law.
Work expands to fill the time available. A proverb worth respecting when timeboxing.
The weekly skeleton: floors first (sleep, exercise, relationships), then one god-mode block, three flow blocks, admin windows, 20% deliberate slack.
Real physiological and clinical change driven by expectation and meaning — demonstrable even with open-label placebos.
The claim that posture changes hormones failed replication — but posture shifts felt power briefly (Ranehill et al., 2015). Enough to start a sentence, not a biology.
Imagining the steps beats imagining the result (Pham & Taylor, 1999 — UCLA, not Stanford). Rehearse the process; skip the applause.
The reticular activating system, a real brainstem arousal/filter structure. Popular '11 million vs 50 bits' numbers are estimates from a 1998 book, not measured science.
The tunneled, judgment-degrading state of wanting under shortage (Mullainathan & Shafir). Desperation is a signal-scrambler; clarity of want is the repair.
Belief → expectation → behavior → outcome → confirmation. Runs your life either deliberately or by default.
Quarterly removal of everything that isn't earning its attention rent. Before adding anything, remove one thing.
The physics term borrowed for 'every version of you exists.' A metaphor, named as one: possible selves become real one decision at a time.
EEG frequencies linked to relaxed focus; associated with hypnotic suggestibility (Sabourin et al., 1990). The 'programming before age 7' claims go beyond the evidence.
Giving a task a frame — 25 to 90 minutes — and closing the loop when the box ends. Attention works better with borders.
A scheduled alignment review: results vs plan, assumptions tested, one adjustment maximum. The plan is a hypothesis, not a promise.
Shrink any habit's start to under two minutes. The first rep is the only decision that matters.
Gay Hendricks' framework: self-image regulates results like a thermostat, triggering self-sabotage above the ceiling. Useful psychology; a framework, not a finding.
The claim that 'wanting nothing' pulls outcomes to you. As physics: unsupported. As psychology: bandwidth, clarity and non-attachment — use the psychology.
Write the block's specific output → execute → check off → say the outcome aloud. Completion is a psychological event; bank the win.
The claim that unfinished tasks are remembered ~90% better failed replication. What survived: the pull to resume (Ovsiankina) and plan-making's ability to discharge an open loop.
The minimum version of a behavior that still counts. Below the floor, no day is ever zero.
